reason: known-bad control 'first_dependency_only' was ACCEPTED (should have been rejected by the hidden suite)

checks.description: Reference solution scores (1.0, True) identically across 3 repeated grades.
The unmodified snapshot passes regression, fails the hidden suite (T_hidden=0.000), and scores 0.0 / functional_pass=False, as required.

Task uses an editable_paths allow-list, which makes gate 7 (no editable, unprotected oracle-helper import) hold structurally: any local module the hidden/regression suites import that isn't the editable code-under-test is already unreachable by any diff without failing the scope gate.
All 11 protected-path/allow-list probes correctly flagged a scope violation. One known, documented gap (a `_pytest/` shadow package) was also probed and confirmed — see findings.

1/4 declared control(s) did NOT match their declared expectation via a genuine hidden-test verdict: first_dependency_only. A known-bad solution that is accepted, or a valid alternative that is rejected by the hidden suite, is direct evidence the oracle is either too permissive or too narrow.
All 1 sampled artifact(s) graded identically across their repeats.

controls.name: first_dependency_only
controls.description: Realistic incomplete-loop bug: only the FIRST dependency in each node's dependency list is wired into the graph; any additional dependencies in the same list are silently ignored (e.g. written as `deps[0]` instead of iterating the whole list). Cycle detection and lexicographic tiebreaks are otherwise implemented correctly. This is exactly the failure mode the hidden test_multiple_implicit_dependencies docstring calls out ('an impl that registers only the FIRST implicit dep of each list misses core').

controls.name: insertion_order_tiebreak
controls.description: Realistic tiebreak bug: dependency ordering and cycle detection are both correct (BFS/Kahn-style with a FIFO queue), but ties between simultaneously-eligible nodes are broken by first-seen/insertion order while scanning the graph, instead of the required lexicographic order. This is the kind of mistake an agent makes by reaching for a plain queue instead of noticing the spec's determinism requirement. The hidden exact-order tests must reject this.

controls.name: missing_cycle_check
controls.description: Realistic 'forgot the edge case' bug: implements Kahn's algorithm correctly for acyclic graphs (min-heap over ready nodes for lexicographic tiebreaks) but never checks whether every node was actually emitted. On a cyclic graph the nodes stuck in the cycle simply never become ready and are silently dropped from the result instead of raising CycleError -- no infinite loop, just a shorter, wrong, non-exception return. The hidden cycle-detection tests must reject this.

controls.name: dfs_postorder
controls.description: Behaviorally equivalent to the reference but structurally different: a depth-first postorder traversal with white/gray/black recursion-stack coloring for cycle detection, instead of the reference's Kahn's-algorithm BFS with a min-heap. Determinism is achieved by visiting the outer node loop and each node's dependency list in sorted (lexicographic) order rather than by a heap of ready nodes. Produces the same dependency-respecting, lexicographically tie-broken order as the reference on every graph shape exercised by the hidden suite.

findings.summary: A `_pytest/` package directory is not flagged as a protected-path violation, though grading runs pytest with the cleanroom at sys.path[0].
findings.detail: Injecting 'graphkit/_pytest/__init__.py' was NOT flagged as touching a protected path. ALWAYS_PROTECTED_BASENAMES matches basenames, not directory names, so a submission-created `_pytest/` package shadowing the real `_pytest` internals package is currently only stopped by this task's editable_paths allow-list (when configured), not by a structural guarantee. See docs/agents/ORACLE.md for why this is reported rather than silently fixed here.

limitations: Grading executes submitted/mutated code via LocalSandbox, which provides per-run workspace isolation and timeouts but NOT untrusted-agent security isolation (runner/afa_runner/sandbox.py's own module docstring). Every check in this report assumes the code being graded is trying to game the SCORE, not attack the HOST — see isolation.hidden_test_readability for a concrete, always-present consequence of that assumption.
Mutation testing, a determinism sample over declared controls, and the isolation probe were not run (QUICK mode) — run --full for stronger evidence.

Mutation equivalence is undecidable in general; a surviving mutant is reported as-is unless explicitly declared equivalent in tasks/<id>/integrity/integrity.json. A mutation kill rate is never treated as a correctness probability (mission §16).
